lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Transfer, reflection, and publication: two-step reasoning in daily planning

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different setting than the problems below.

items.prompt: A theater sets up 5 rows of 8 chairs, then adds 6 more chairs. How many chairs in all?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A store arranges 3 shelves with 4 boxes on each shelf, then adds 5 more boxes to the display. How many boxes are on display now?
A store arranges 8 shelves with 6 boxes on each shelf, then sells 11 boxes from the display. How many boxes are left?
A store arranges 3 shelves with 4 boxes on each shelf, then adds 9 more boxes to the display. How many boxes are on display now?
A store arranges 4 shelves with 4 boxes on each shelf, then adds 7 more boxes to the display. How many boxes are on display now?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: A store arranges 8 shelves with 8 boxes on each shelf, then adds 8 more boxes to the display. How many boxes are on display now?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A store arranges 3 shelves with 3 boxes on each shelf, then sells 13 boxes from the display. How many boxes are left?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
